topics.description: A series of aristocratic, parliamentary, and popular rebellions in France from 1648 to 1653 during the minority of Louis XIV.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This ruler was forced to return the Maastricht to the Netherlands in the Treaties of Nijmegen [nigh-MAY-guhn]. This ruler’s so-called “daughters” were women recruited to populate a New World colony. Jean-Baptiste Colbert was a minister of this ruler. In addition to starting the War of Devolution, this ruler faced a rebellion of noblemen and Parliament, called the Fronde, who opposed Cardinal (*) Mazarin. Many Huguenots were displaced after this ruler issued the 1685 Edict of Fontainebleau, which revoked the Edict of Nantes. The Palace of Versailles [vair-SIGH] was ordered to be constructed by, for 10 points, what longest-ruling “Sun King” of France?
parts.answer: Louis XIV [the 14th] [or Louis the Great; or Louis le Grand; prompt on the Sun King before mention; prompt on Louis]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country was forbidden from allying with Spain in the Peace of Utrecht. Nobles of this country attempted to dethrone a boy king in a rebellion called the Fronde. This officially Catholic country persecuted the (*) Huguenots after the Edict of Fontainebleau. The palace of Versailles was once a royal residence in, for ten points, what country led by the “Sun King,” Louis XIV [fourteenth]?
parts.answer: France (accept Kingdom of France; accept Royaume de France)

topics.description: Venetian merchant and traveler whose visit to Kublai Khan's court and account of Yuan China introduced influential descriptions of Asia to medieval European audiences.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about Kublai Khan, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Kublai Khan founded this dynasty of China. Revolts by the Han majority led to this dynasty being replaced by the Ming Dynasty.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Kublai Khan received this traveler as a visitor to his court. While imprisoned, this Italian wrote a book describing the wonders of Kublai Khan’s court for Western audiences.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Kublai Khan’s mainland campaigns were largely successful, but his two invasions of Japan were each thwarted by typhoons, described in Japanese by this term, meaning “divine wind.”

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After this ruler defeated his brother, Ariq Böke, he conquered one region after the Battle of Yamen. This  leader’s attempted invasions of Japan were stopped by a “divine wind," or kamikaze. While he was emperor  of a (*) Chinese dynasty, this leader’s court was visited by the Venetian merchant Marco Polo. For 10 points, name  this Mongol ruler of the Yuan Dynasty, the grandson of Genghis.
parts.answer: Kublai Khan [or Emperor Shizu of Yuan]

topics.description: The United Kingdom is the sovereign state in northwestern Europe comprising England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
aliases: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s Conservative Party went into crisis in July 2022. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country, whose Prime Minister Boris Johnson resigned after suffering a record 62 cabinet resignations within the span of two days.
parts.answer: United Kingdom (or Great Britain; prompt on England)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This successor to Johnson as Prime Minister was on a plane to Indonesia during the onset of the crisis. This former Foreign Secretary was criticized in 2016 for her opposition to Brexit, though she later supported it.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In October 2022, this man became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. This former Chancellor of the Exchequer was among the first in Johnson’s cabinet to resign as a result of the Chris Pincher scandal.

topics.description: The 1937–1938 campaign of mass killing, rape, and other atrocities committed by Japanese forces in and around Nanjing, China.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: During a massacre by this country’s army, Nazi party member John Rabe set up a “Safety Zone” to protect civilians. The U.S. refused to prosecute scientists from this country’s Unit 731 in exchange for its data from testing biological weapons on live prisoners. This country invaded its neighbor under the pretext of the Marco Polo Bridge Incident. This country’s army employed thousands of “comfort women” who were forced into sexual slavery; its army also killed around 200,000 civilians during the “Rape of Nanjing.” For 10 points, name this country that committed many war crimes under Emperor Hirohito.
parts.answer: Japan [or Nihon-koku; or Nippon-koku; or Empire of Japan; or Dai Nippon Teikoku; or Japanese Empire]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This person's two terms, the last concluding in 2020, made him the longest-serving Japanese prime  minister. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this politician who was assassinated in 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] As a motive, Abe's suspected assassin denounced the politician's connections to this Christian  offshoot church. It was founded by Sun Myung Moon and has extensive ties to conservative politics in  both Japan and the U.S.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Abe co-wrote a document that largely denied the historical existence of this 1937 atrocity for which  general Iwane Matsui (ee-wah-nay maht-soo-ee) was executed on war crimes charges.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Nanjing Massacre [or Nanking Massacre; or Rape of Nanjing; or Rape of Nanking]

topics.description: A Central European country whose historical and modern identity is associated with Warsaw, the partitions of Poland, the May 3rd Constitution, and major sites such as Świebodzin.

parts.label: L
parts.question: May 3rd, 1791 saw the adoption of the world’s second-ever modern constitution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] The constitution was adopted by the “commonwealth” between this country and its northern neighbor Lithuania. Soon after, this country was partitioned three times among its neighbors.
parts.answer: Poland [accept Commonwealth of Poland; accept Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The May 3rd Constitution was inspired by this other country’s constitution, which was written in 1787 to replace its Articles of Confederation.
parts.answer: United States of America [or U.S.A; accept any underlined portion]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The May 3rd Constitution was nullified due to Russian bribery at a 1793 meeting of this parliament of the Commonwealth. It shares its name with the lower house of Poland’s modern-day parliament.

topics.description: The Tamil people are a Dravidian ethnolinguistic group concentrated in Tamil Nadu and northern and eastern Sri Lanka.

parts.label: L
parts.question: During this conflict, a group fought to establish an ethnic homeland, in a territory the organization  called “Eelam” (EE-lahm). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this conflict that began in 1983 and was fought between a group led by Velupillai  Prabhakaran (VEL-oo-pil-ai preb-AH-kuh-run) and a government dominated by the Sinhalese (SIN-uh- leez) ethnicity.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This ethnic group's “Liberation Tigers” fought against the Sinhalese government in Sri Lanka until  its surrender in 2009.
parts.answer: Tamils (TAH-milz) [or Tamilar; or Tamilians; or Tamil Tigers]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Tamil Tigers assassinated Rajiv, an Indian prime minister with this surname. Rajiv was the son  of Indira, another assassinated Indian prime minister with this surname.

topics.description: Blackbeard was an infamous early-eighteenth-century pirate who commanded the Queen Anne’s Revenge and later the Adventure in the Caribbean and along the eastern coast of North America.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Period romances have recently surged in popularity. Identify some ongoing romantic TV series, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This Regency-era Netflix series produced by Shondaland is based on romance novels by Julia Quinn. It stars Golda Rosheuvel as a Black Queen Charlotte overseeing the dramatics of the title family.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This Regency-era PBS show is based on an unfinished Jane Austen novel, and follows the dramatic romance of Charlotte Heywood and Sidney Parker in a title seaside resort.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Breaking with the strong trend for Regency drama, the HBO comedy Our Flag Means Death follows the romance of Stede Bonnet and this real-life pirate, who captained the Queen Anne’s Revenge.
parts.answer: Blackbeard (accept either underlined portion of Edward Teach; accept Edward Thatch)

topics.description: A heavily fortified buffer zone established near the 38th parallel after the Korean War to separate North Korea and South Korea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader had his uncle executed for treason in 2013 and likely ordered the assassination of his half-brother in early 2017. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this leader who met with Donald Trump to discuss denuclearization at a 2018 summit in Singapore.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Kim Jong-un is the Supreme Leader of the northern, communist half of this peninsula. The southern, democratic half of this peninsula is led by President Moon Jae-in.
parts.answer: Korean Peninsula (accept North and/or South Korea)

parts.label: C
parts.question: After the Korean War, one of these areas was established along the thirty-eighth parallel, the border between North and South Korea. Despite its name, both sides of this area are heavily guarded by soldiers.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Two answers required. The “Peace Village” is on the border between these two countries, which was created by a 1953 armistice signed in Panmunjom. The Sunshine Policy attempts to improve relations between these two countries. The 38th parallel was used to demarcate (*) the Demilitarized Zone that separates, for 10 points, what two Asian nations that share a peninsula that contains cities like Seoul and Pyongyang?

topics.description: The Korean dynasty founded in 1392 that ruled Korea until the establishment of the Korean Empire in 1897, with the broader Joseon royal order ending under Japanese annexation in 1910.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A kingdom in this region was dominated for a time by a faction known as the Sarim. That kingdom from this region was home to a research institute known as the Hall of Worthies and was dominated by an elite class known as the yangban. A military commander employed by a kingdom in this region designed so-called (*) “turtle ships” to counter the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; that commander was Yi Sun-Sin. Sejong the Great ruled the kingdom of Joseon, which dominated this region for five centuries. For 10 points, name this region now split between two countries governed from Pyongyang and Seoul.
parts.answer: Korean peninsula [accept South Korea or Republic of Korea or North Korea or Democratic People’s Republic of Korea or Hanguk or Joseon]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This region’s rule by Empress Min in the late 19th century led a Western scholar to call it a “hermit kingdom.” In 1598, the Ming Dynasty helped defend this region against an invading fleet at the Battle of Noryang. In the thirteenth century, this region’s (*) Goryeo Dynasty fell to Kublai Khan, and its Joseon dynasty ended in 1897 with its invasion by Japan. For ten points, name this East Asian peninsula that is, today, split into two countries.
parts.answer: Korea (accept Korean Peninsula; accept Koryo until “Goryeo” is read; accept North and South Korea only after “today” is read)

topics.description: Norwegian polar explorer who led the first successful expedition to reach the South Pole in 1911.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about polar expeditions that used the ship Fram:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott’s by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.
parts.answer: Roald Amundsen (“ROH-all AW-moon-sen”) [or Roald Engelbregt Gravning Amundsen; accept Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] The Fram was earlier used by this other Norwegian explorer for his 1893 Arctic expedition. This explorer won the Nobel Peace Prize for his namesake passports, which the League of Nations issued to stateless refugees.
parts.answer: Fridtjof Nansen (“FRIT-yoff NAWN-sin”) [or Fridtjof Wedel-Jarlsberg Nansen; accept Nansen passports]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Fellow Norwegian Otto Sverdrup (“AW-toh SVAR-droop”) led an 1898 expedition to the Arctic islands of this country aboard the Fram. The Norse settlement of Vinland was in this North American country’s province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The last words of one person attempting to reach this location were “I'm just going outside and may be some time.” The Endurance and Nimrod expeditions to reach this location were captained by Ernest Shackleton. After attempting to use horses to reach this location, Robert Smith was beaten to this location by the Norwegian explorer Roald (*) Amundsen. For ten points, name this location near the center of Antarctica..
